viewer_sees: At first light, Spanish sailors pry planks from the broken hull of a wrecked ship lying on a sandbank, carrying them up the beach to a rough wooden tower rising on a low mound; nobody else is there
ANIMATED MAP — on an aged parchment of the Caribbean, three small ship markers sail in from the east; one peels away toward the south and fades, the other two keep going to a large island

Two Spanish ships, a tall round-hulled flagship and a small lateen-rigged caravel, glide along a green mountainous coast at dawn while Columbus stands at the flagship's rail and a native dugout canoe paddles out toward them

A ship's boat grounds on the beach below a Taino town; villagers walk up from a swept clean square carrying baskets of food and gourds of drink to the Spaniards, and the chief lifts his hand to ask them to stay
Night: the flagship drifts along a dark coast on glassy water, her sails hanging slack under a full moon, a single lantern lit at the stern
Columbus, grey with exhaustion, climbs down the hatch from the deck into a low lamplit cabin and sinks onto his narrow bunk
On the moonlit deck the helmsman steps away from the long tiller bar and walks aft toward the hatch, leaving a small young crewman gripping the bar alone
The flagship's bow slides softly onto a pale sandbank in moonlight, a white line of surf ahead; the deck stays quiet and a tiny figure at the stern throws up his arms
Columbus points hard toward the stern anchor and shouts orders; the master and a few sailors lower the ship's boat, climb in and row away across the moonlit water toward the small caravel's lantern
The caravel's crew stand along her rail and turn the boat away; the flagship leans over on her side on the sandbank, planks starting to split open at the waterline
At dawn Guacanagari stands on the beach looking at the wreck with his hand at his chest; dugout canoes then cross the water to the leaning ship and carry barrels, chests and bundles ashore
Guacanagari shows Columbus two large thatched houses at the edge of his town, then points with a long steady arm toward blue mountains inland while Columbus follows the gesture
On the beach the chief points out to sea where narrow canoes of raiders are paddling; Columbus listens with one hand resting on his sword hilt and nods slowly
Five lesser chiefs, each in a gold crown, walk up the beach to the town; Guacanagari lifts his own crown from his head and places it on Columbus's head
MACRO OBJECT — on a woven mat lie a collar of coloured beads, a fine red cloak, a pair of coloured boots and a silver ring; the chief's hand reaches in, lifts the ring and turns it in the light
Columbus writes in his journal by lantern light; then, an empty beach with no one on it as a single caravel sails away past the headland
The small caravel rides at anchor off the shore; on the sand a ring of crewmen crowd around Columbus, raising their hands and pointing inland toward the hills
Spanish sailors and island workers drag planks and beams from the wreck up to a mound, where a wooden tower and a palisade of upright logs are going up
Columbus sits at a plain table in a thatched house, quill moving across a journal page; through the open doorway islanders go about their day in the sunlit square
Columbus steps from a boat onto the beach to take leave of the chief; then a cannon fires into the wreck's hull in a burst of smoke while armed Spanish crews skirmish on the sand
Guacanagari and Columbus stand side by side watching the staged fight; the chief's face is grave and unreadable, Columbus's face is satisfied, smoke drifting across the beach
The chief lowers his eyes in sorrow; then one of his relatives raises a flat hand to the height of Columbus's head to show the size of a golden statue while Columbus listens
LEDGER/ACCUMULATION — casks of wine, sacks of bread, bundles of trade goods, a small cannon and the ship's boat are unloaded and stacked higher and higher on the sand beside the new fort
A clerk holds up a long handwritten list of names; then a carpenter with an adze, a gunner with a linstock, a doctor with a satchel and a tailor with shears stand in a row before the fort gate
Three men stand at the fort gate looking inland toward the mountains while far out on the water the small caravel sails away with sails full
A fleet of seventeen ships under full sail glides toward a dark island coast at dusk, three loose rows of sails across the water
At night a cannon fires from the flagship's deck, a flash of flame and smoke over black water; Columbus and his officers turn their heads toward the dark shore and wait; no light and no answer comes
EMPTY AFTERMATH — in morning light a bare stretch of beach with grass already growing over a clearing where houses once stood, a torn scrap of cloth moving in the wind
The burned shell of the fort: blackened posts and a fallen tower on the mound, smoke thinning, ravens circling over a trampled field where a few dark shapes lie in the far grass
Guacanagari lies in his hammock in a dim thatched house and speaks slowly to a circle of listening Spanish officers

ANIMATED MAP — on a parchment of Hispaniola the small fort icon on the north coast: one man-marker dims, a group walks inland to a mountain mark and stops there, then the fort icon itself flares and burns
In the fort's main house by firelight a handful of Spanish sailors quarrel over a heap of gold ornaments, grabbing each other's collars across the table
MACRO OBJECT — a Spanish scribe's hand writes a page with a quill; the opposite half of the table is bare wood with a carved wooden stool and an empty clay bowl
Guacanagari in half-light, one side of his face in shadow, looking straight ahead with an unreadable expression
Guacanagari gestures toward his town while Columbus stands on a path that bends toward distant mountains, watching him with narrowed eyes
Columbus and Guacanagari face each other across a woven mat; on Columbus's side a small heap of gold ornaments, on the chief's side a carved war club
Archaeologists in sun hats kneel in square trenches on a grassy mound, then close on what they uncover: charred posts, shards of pottery, a lead ball and small bones
One archaeologist stands at the edge of the trench with a trowel in her hand, looking down into the dark postholes at dusk
PROCESS/CUTAWAY — a cross-section of the coast: a green meadow on top, layers of earth beneath, and deep under them the pale ribs of a buried ship
A weathered timber lies half-buried in grass on a green meadow with the sea beyond; the camera pulls back until it is one small mark among many that look alike
END CARD
